answer: Give every identity a place on a whisper graph, where edges form only through sustained witnessed exchanges. Influence grows as an agent nears trusted anchor nodes, and each step inward costs real time. A lone umber thread proves nothing; standing comes from distinct neighbors over many epochs. Sybils betray themselves by clustering: dozens of accounts sharing the same few edges, the same timing, the same saffron-stained shortcuts, all at the same distance from every anchor. No copied history fakes a wide, slow-grown neighborhood; mass fakery pays the same slow cost as honest growth.
